title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: automatic preservation of deleted content for high-risk users
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates who can discover preserved content and incorrectly calls the feature-specific setting the only documented off switch. Its claim that changes are portal-only also goes beyond the documentation; the retention behaviour and roadmap details are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans automatic retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on insider risk.
claims.quote: The integration with Data Lifecycle Management will automatically apply retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user’s insider risk level.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection moves users into and out of policies as their insider risk levels change.
claims.quote: automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk levels change over time

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2024.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2024"

claims.claim: General Availability and Preview are the roadmap release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.quote: In preview, you can use this solution with Insider Risk Management so that retention labels are automatically applied with Adaptive Protection.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The integration automatically labels deleted SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content for users assigned the Elevated insider risk level.
claims.quote: the data lifecycle management policy monitors users that assign an Elevated risk level by Insider Risk Management Adaptive Protection. When a risky user deletes any content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange Online, the contents are automatically preserved for 120 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales; changes
claims.claim: The automatic retention period is 120 days.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.claim: The label is applied to unlabelled content rather than content that already has a retention label.
claims.quote: retention labels are automatically applied to unlabeled content if it's deleted by users who have been identified as an elevated risk.

claims.claim: Users do not see the automatically applied retention label.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: Items become eligible for permanent deletion after the 120 days expire.
claims.quote: After the 120 days expire, the items then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Administrators cannot currently change this retention period.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period

claims.claim: Administrators cannot currently assign different retention policies for different risk levels.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot currently assign different retention policies for different locations.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Preserved content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery in the workload's secured locations.
claims.quote: As a result, that content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery from the secured locations used by the workload.

claims.claim: Anyone with eDiscovery access can find the preserved items.
claims.quote: This role lets users access review sets in eDiscovery. ... This role doesn't allow the user to preview the results of a search that's associated with the case or do other search or case management tasks.
claims.fix: Replace 'Anyone with eDiscovery access can therefore find items the user thought were deleted.' with 'The preserved content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery from the secured locations used by the workload.' This wording is supported by the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention and makes no blanket permissions claim.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Tenants that enabled and configured Adaptive Protection before this integration released must opt in to create the retention policy.
claims.quote: If you enabled and configured Adaptive Protection before this integration with data lifecycle management released, you'll need to opt-in to create this auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: The quick setup documentation says the policy is automatically created and applied when a tenant first turns on Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote: If you haven't already turned on Adaptive Protection, the policy is automatically created and applied when you turn on Adaptive Protection.

claims.claim: The custom setup note says an explicit opt-in is needed to apply the data lifecycle management policy.
claims.quote: If you turn on Adaptive Protection for your organization, you need to explicitly opt in to apply the data lifecycle management policy.

claims.claim: Learn's quick setup and custom setup descriptions differ on automatic application versus explicit opt-in.
claims.quote: the policy is automatically created and applied when you turn on Adaptive Protection. ... If you turn on Adaptive Protection for your organization, you need to explicitly opt in to apply the data lifecycle management policy.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk; changes
claims.claim: The general availability default is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection data lifecycle management general availability default automatic preservation meter pricing. Read roadmap, retention and insider-risk-management-adaptive-protection: preview setup is described, but no distinct GA default is stated.

claims.claim: No source says the general availability release changes existing behaviour for tenants that do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection data lifecycle management general availability default automatic preservation meter pricing. Read roadmap and both feature articles: no no-action GA rollout change is specified; existing adopters are told to opt in.

claims.claim: The retention setting is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Settings > Solution settings > Data lifecycle management > Adaptive protection.
claims.quote: Solutions > Settings > Solution settings> Data lifecycle management > Adaptive protection. ... For Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management, turn the setting off
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Solutions > Settings > Solution settings > Data lifecycle management > Adaptive protection > Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management'. The existing path stops on the correct page but omits the setting itself.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation is documented for the Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection Data Lifecycle Management enable disable PowerShell Graph Set AdaptiveProtection retention; Exchange PowerShell AdaptiveProtection retention. Read retention, retention-cmdlets and Adaptive Protection; no switch operation found.

claims.claim: The tenant Adaptive Protection switch is under Insider Risk Management > Adaptive protection > Adaptive Protection settings > Adaptive Protection in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Go to the Insider Risk Management solution. ... Select Adaptive protection in the left navigation ... To enable Adaptive Protection, select the Adaptive Protection settings tab, and then turn Adaptive Protection to On.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for turning tenant Adaptive Protection on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management Adaptive Protection enable PowerShell Graph; Graph adaptive protection enable insider risk management; PowerShell AdaptiveProtection Set. Read Adaptive Protection configure/disable sections; no operation found.

claims.claim: Audit searches are configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the PowerShell operation for searching the unified audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: The data lifecycle management setting cannot be turned on unless Adaptive Protection is on for the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to turn on this setting unless Adaptive Protection is turned on for your tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off the data lifecycle management setting removes the labels it applied, making items eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Any retention labels that were applied as a result of Adaptive Protection are removed so that the items can then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: Turning off the automatic retention policy does not affect other Adaptive Protection policies.
claims.quote: you can turn off the auto-labeling policy without affecting other Adaptive Protection policies.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Configuring Adaptive Protection and updating its settings requires the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Admins role group.
claims.quote: Configure Adaptive Protection and update settings | Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Admins

claims.claim: Turning off tenant Adaptive Protection stops sharing insider risk levels with data lifecycle management.
claims.quote: If you turn off Adaptive Protection after it's been on and active, the system stops assigning insider risk levels to users and stops sharing them with data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access.

claims.claim: The integration uses a single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy per tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The automatic retention label and policy are not visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Administrators do not need to create or manage this label and auto-labeling policy or approve each labelled deletion.
claims.quote: a retention label is automatically applied to that content ... you don't need to create or manage the retention label or auto-labeling retention policy.

claims.claim: Retained file proactively is the SharePoint and OneDrive event, selectable under Retention policy and retention label activities.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, from Retention policy and retention label activities, select Retained file proactively

claims.claim: Retained email item proactively is the Exchange event, selectable under Retention policy and retention label activities.
claims.quote: For Exchange, from Retention policy and retention label activities, select Retained email item proactively

claims.claim: The proactive retention events identify the user and item being retained.
claims.quote: When these items are retained with Adaptive Protection, the following auditing events are generated and identify the user and item

claims.claim: Audit search requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Quick setup can take up to 72 hours to finish.
claims.quote: After you start the quick setup process, it can take up to 72 hours before the following items are completed

claims.where: Scope: Rollout; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Adaptive Protection actions can take up to 36 hours to apply after it is turned on.
claims.quote: It might take up to 36 hours before you can expect to see Adaptive Protection insider risk levels and data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access actions applied to applicable user activities.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no integration-specific entitlement is published.
claims.quote: Manage insider risk and communication compliance ... Microsoft 365 E5 ... Insider Risk Management, Communication Compliance, Adaptive Protection, and related advanced controls.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the licensing notes with 'Microsoft 365 E5 includes Adaptive Protection. A licence requirement specific to this data lifecycle management integration is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/compare-copilot-e3-e5-e7. Use the same distinction in Cost and licensing and the cost rationale instead of treating all entitlement as unknown.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Adaptive Protection article itself names no licence and refers licensing questions to the Microsoft 365, Office 365, Enterprise Mobility + Security, and Windows 11 Subscriptions page.
claims.quote: To learn about licensing requirements for using Adaptive Protection with data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access, see Microsoft 365, Office 365, Enterprise Mobility + Security, and Windows 11 Subscriptions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; changes
claims.claim: An entitlement requirement specific to this data lifecycle management integration is not published on the feature pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive Protection data lifecycle management automatic retention licensing requirements E5. Read feature articles, Purview service description and E3/E5/E7 comparison; found general product entitlement, not an integration SKU.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature documentation publishes no separate automatic-retention price, meter or per-use charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection data lifecycle management general availability default automatic preservation meter pricing; Adaptive Protection data lifecycle meter. Read feature articles and Purview service description; no separate preservation rate or meter found.

claims.claim: The Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management setting is the only documented off switch.
claims.quote: To disable Adaptive Protection, select the Adaptive Protection settings tab and turn Adaptive Protection Off. ... the system stops assigning insider risk levels to users and stops sharing them with data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access.
claims.fix: Replace 'the only documented off switch is the Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management setting' with 'the feature-specific off switch is the Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management setting'. The tenant-wide Adaptive Protection switch is also documented, including in the briefing's second control row.

claims.claim: Changes to the retention setting are portal-only.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection Data Lifecycle Management enable disable PowerShell Graph Set AdaptiveProtection retention. Read retention, retention-cmdlets and Adaptive Protection; no statement rules out other surfaces.
claims.fix: Delete ', so changes are portal-only' from the first sentence. Keep the narrower, verified statement that Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Graph operation for the setting at the time of writing.

claims.claim: Audit search is the monitoring route the cited pages document for this feature, with no alternative item-retention monitoring route described there.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive Protection data lifecycle management monitoring audit dashboard. Read retention, Adaptive Protection management/dashboard sections and audit-search; only audit search is described for identifying proactively retained items.

claims.claim: Data lifecycle management metrics do not currently appear on the Adaptive Protection dashboard.
claims.quote: Data lifecycle management metrics don't currently appear on the dashboard.

claims.claim: A user's deletion can proceed while the integration retains the content without showing the retention label to the user.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days. ... users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to review the Elevated-risk population, but the controls table has no corresponding user-risk review control.
claims.quote: Review who sits at the Elevated risk level, since that population decides whose deletions are held. ... Controls cover automatic retention, the tenant Adaptive Protection switch, and audit records.
claims.fix: The checklist step 'Review who sits at the Elevated risk level, since that population decides whose deletions are held' has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove that step from the checklist; this correction does not require adding a row.
